citation: Çelik, Çam & Koseoglu — Ad avoidance in the digital context
method_sample: Systematic review; 56 articles and 62 studies through 2021
key_finding: Digital ad avoidance has multiple antecedents, mediators, moderators, and behavioral forms; the evidence base is fragmented.
limitation: Review stops at 2021 and pools heterogeneous media and measures.
ad_mind_use: Use a multi-causal avoidance model; do not treat skipping as the only negative outcome.

citation: Goodrich, Schiller & Galletta — Consumer Reactions to Intrusiveness of Online-Video Advertisements
method_sample: Experimental study; sample size not reported in accessible record
key_finding: Intrusiveness harmed attitudes and intentions toward both advertiser and host; informativeness, humor, and length affected perceived intrusion.
limitation: Study setting and sample details require publisher access; result does not imply longer is always better.
ad_mind_use: Score host-platform harm separately and pretest creative characteristics.

citation: Chen & Zhou — Avoiding pre-roll ads: Predictors of online video consumption
method_sample: National Chinese survey; N=513; SEM
key_finding: Prior negative experience, perceived goal obstacles, ad length, clutter, and presence of others predicted avoidance.
limitation: Self-reported avoidance and China-specific compulsory pre-roll setting.
ad_mind_use: Add goal impediment, clutter, length, and social context to interruption cost.

citation: Brechman, Bellman, Robinson, Rask & Varan — Limited-Interruption Advertising in Digital-Video Content
method_sample: Experimental comparison of limited-interruption mid-roll, pre-roll, clutter, and repetition; sample not in accessible abstract
key_finding: Placement and repeated single-ad breaks create both positive and negative advertising effects.
limitation: Accessible abstract does not expose the complete design and effect sizes.
ad_mind_use: Treat placement and repeated limited interruption as testable policies rather than fixed rules.

citation: Belanche, Flavián & Pérez-Rueda — Understanding Interactive Online Advertising
method_sample: Pretest plus three studies of skippable video ads
key_finding: High-arousal ads were watched longer and were more effective in congruent contexts; product involvement moderated intrusiveness.
limitation: Multiple controlled studies but platform, creative, and involvement effects may not generalize to all video.
ad_mind_use: Model arousal, congruity, and involvement separately.

citation: Choi & Kim — The impacts of ad skip option and ad time display
method_sample: 2×2 online experiment; Qualtrics N=217
key_finding: Skip and time display increased perceived control, lowering intrusiveness and irritation and improving ad attitude.
limitation: Single online experiment; attitudes are not long-term retention or revenue.
ad_mind_use: Test behavioral control and temporal information as separate features.

citation: Jeon, Son, Chung & Drumwright — Temporal Certainty and Skippable In-Stream Commercials
method_sample: Two experiments varying ad length, timer, and skip
key_finding: A timer generally reduced irritation for short ads, but with a skip button it increased irritation for both short and long ads; irritation predicted skipping.
limitation: Experimental creatives and timing combinations limit universalization.
ad_mind_use: Do not assume countdown plus skip is always helpful; test interaction effects.

citation: Riedel, Weeks & Beatson — Dealing with intrusive ads
method_sample: Three experiment sets; Experiment 1A N=134, 2A N=121, 2B N=135 plus additional preference/choice studies
key_finding: Skip improved preference but reduced memory; countdown to ad end and choice of when to view produced the strongest joint outcomes.
limitation: Mostly MTurk/controlled exposure; brand memory and preference are only part of platform value.
ad_mind_use: Offer schedule choice; track preference and memory as separate outcomes.

citation: Frade, Oliveira & Giraldi — Skippable or non-skippable? Pre-roll or mid-roll?
method_sample: 2×2 experiment with eye-tracking; N=157 reported in related full-text discussion
key_finding: Non-skippable and pre-roll conditions produced stronger visual attention/effectiveness; skippable viewers focused heavily on the skip region; mid-roll was more intrusive.
limitation: Lab-style exposure and regional 15-second format; forced attention may not imply long-term value.
ad_mind_use: Measure attention allocation to controls and compare pre-roll/mid-roll trade-offs.

citation: Vermeulen, Droog & Burgers — Overlay ads in humorous online videos
method_sample: Two four-condition experiments; N=109 and N=394
key_finding: Overlay at the punch line reduced recall/recognition, while simultaneous or just-before placement sometimes improved attitude and purchase intention.
limitation: Humorous Dutch stand-up videos and one soda brand; objectives moved in opposite directions.
ad_mind_use: Use scene-level timing and advertiser objective, not only placement type.

citation: Jiang, Guan & de Haaij — Congruity and Processing Fluency
venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
method_sample: 2×2×2 online experiment; N=252
key_finding: Ad-video and product-video congruity improved processing fluency only for informational appeals; fluency improved attitudes.
limitation: Mock embedded videos; congruity effect did not generalize to emotional appeals.
ad_mind_use: Apply semantic-fit bonuses conditionally by creative appeal.

citation: Thavorn, Trichob, Klongthong & Ngamkroeckjoti — Effect of mid-roll video advertising value
method_sample: Survey of Thai Facebook users; N=200; CFA/SEM
key_finding: Perceived value improved attitude and word of mouth; perceived intrusiveness harmed attitude.
limitation: Retrospective single-country Facebook sample, heavily aged 25–34; correlational design.
ad_mind_use: Keep ad utility/value and intrusiveness as separate dimensions.

citation: Pashkevich, Dorai-Raj, Kellar & Zigmond — Empowering Online Advertisements by Empowering Viewers
method_sample: Google/YouTube randomized experiments and search-lift effectiveness measure
key_finding: Skippable TrueView ads could be as effective per impression as conventional ads and showed strong implied viewer preference.
limitation: Industry-authored study, historical YouTube product, and proprietary outcome definition.
ad_mind_use: Include an industry precedent for choice, but reproduce with transparent metrics.

citation: Li & Yin — How perceived control affects advertising avoidance intention
method_sample: Chinese-context survey; SEM and conditional process analysis
key_finding: Perceived control reduced avoidance; intrusiveness partially mediated; ad content quality moderated the pathway.
limitation: Survey intention rather than observed behavior; sample size not exposed in accessible abstract.
ad_mind_use: Let control alter interruption cost, moderated by creative quality.

citation: Shon, Shin, Hwang & Lee — Free contents vs. inconvenience costs
method_sample: Conjoint survey, mixed logit, and platform market-share simulation
key_finding: Use of personal information produced the largest inconvenience cost; shorter ads and less personal-data use improved simulated platform share.
limitation: Stated-preference and simulation results are not observed churn or revenue.
ad_mind_use: Represent privacy/data-use as an explicit viewer cost, not only a compliance flag.

citation: Furini — A multimedia framework for personalized, non-intrusive advertising in video streaming
method_sample: Proof of concept plus questionnaire; N=104 young adults
key_finding: User-activated overlays linked to on-screen products attracted interest and offered a lightweight alternative to forced interruption.
limitation: Young, narrow sample and proof-of-concept environment; no production platform test.
ad_mind_use: Prototype a pull-based contextual card/overlay as an optional format.

citation: Kwon, King, Nyilasy & Reid — Impact of Media Context on Advertising Memory
method_sample: Meta-analysis of quantitative media-context studies through 2013
key_finding: Context factors had significant but weak-to-moderate relationships with advertising memory; context should inform media decisions.
limitation: Memory focus, older corpus, and correlated context/study factors; not a simple congruity rule.
ad_mind_use: Use context as one input and retain uncertainty/boundary conditions.

citation: Calder, Malthouse & Schaedel — Online Engagement and Advertising Effectiveness
method_sample: Experiments using scales across eight online experiences
key_finding: Personal and social-interactive engagement with a site were positively associated with banner-ad effectiveness.
limitation: Website/banner context predates modern streaming; construct measurement may not transfer directly.
ad_mind_use: Include media engagement as a possible amplifier, not a license to interrupt.

citation: Hühn et al. — Does location congruence matter?
method_sample: Four-week experience-sampling field experiment; 40 recruited, 23 responding, 107 responses
key_finding: Location congruity raised relevance and value but did not reduce intrusiveness; intra-person variation was substantial.
limitation: Small student campus sample and restaurant coupons.
ad_mind_use: Do not let a relevance gain automatically cancel interruption cost.

citation: Sharma — Recall of television commercials as a function of viewing context
method_sample: 2×2 experiment; N=103
key_finding: Cognitive ads were recalled better in cognitive programs and affective ads in affective programs.
limitation: Traditional TV and immediate recall; not interactive or personalized delivery.
ad_mind_use: Distinguish informational versus affective fit in scene/ad matching.

citation: Furnham, Gunter & Richardson — Effects of Product–Program Congruity
method_sample: Youth experiment; N=123 aged 16–19; car and food ads/programs
key_finding: Memory results depended on free versus cued recall and sometimes favored incongruity; involvement was unrelated to recall/recognition.
limitation: Youth sample, traditional TV, limited categories.
ad_mind_use: Prevent a universal congruity bonus and evaluate multiple memory outcomes.

citation: Tafani, Roux & Greifeneder — In the mood for action
method_sample: Three experiments; judgment, intention, and event-attendance outcomes
key_finding: Negative program-induced mood increased bottom-up processing of strong arguments and produced higher behavioral effectiveness in the tested condition.
limitation: Effect depends on argument quality and study setting; not permission to target distress.
ad_mind_use: Avoid a simplistic positive-mood rule; protected distress remains a separate hard policy.

citation: Kamins, Marks & Skinner — Television Commercial Evaluation in Program-Induced Mood
method_sample: Program-induced mood/commercial evaluation experiment; sample not reported in accessible record
key_finding: Commercial evaluation depended on program-induced mood and mood-message relationship.
limitation: Older television study; full design/effect sizes not audited.
ad_mind_use: Represent mood fit as uncertain contextual evidence rather than a deterministic rule.

citation: Zhu & Chang — The key role of relevance in personalized advertisement
method_sample: Survey of online users; N=386
key_finding: Perceived relevance mitigated privacy concerns and improved continued-use intention, while privacy invasion reduced it.
limitation: Cross-sectional perceptions and intentions; relevance does not erase consent requirements.
ad_mind_use: Keep relevance and privacy risk in separate score components.

citation: Bleier & Eisenbeiss — Personalized Online Advertising Effectiveness
method_sample: Two large field experiments and two lab experiments; one field sample about 1.2M impressions
key_finding: High personalization was strongest just after a store visit in an early information state and decayed quickly; placement/browsing mode changed informativeness and intrusiveness.
limitation: Retail banners and one partner context; not long-form video.
ad_mind_use: Use signal recency, decision stage, and placement fit; avoid static user profiles.

citation: Lambrecht & Tucker — When Does Retargeting Work?
method_sample: Online travel-firm field experiment covering 2.8M+ exposed consumers plus robustness experiments
key_finding: Specific dynamic retargeting underperformed generic ads on average until behavior indicated narrowed preferences.
limitation: Travel category and historic banner environment; observed external browsing is an imperfect stage proxy.
ad_mind_use: Do not equate the most specific available creative with the best choice.

citation: Aguirre, Mahr, Grewal, de Ruyter & Wetzels — Unraveling the personalization paradox
method_sample: Exploratory Facebook field evidence, campaign secondary data, and three experiments
key_finding: Covert information collection increased vulnerability and could sharply reduce click-through; overt collection and trust cues mitigated the effect.
limitation: Facebook/retail setting and mixed evidence sources; not a substitute for current legal review.
ad_mind_use: Record signal provenance and consent visibility; explain why data are used.

citation: Bleier & Eisenbeiss — The Importance of Trust for Personalized Online Advertising
method_sample: Quasi-experimental retargeting field data plus scenario-based lab experiment
key_finding: Trusted retailers benefited from high-depth/narrow-breadth personalization; for less trusted retailers high depth triggered reactance/privacy concern.
limitation: Retailer trust and banner personalization may not transfer directly to a video platform.
ad_mind_use: Include advertiser/platform trust and breadth/depth limits.

citation: White, Zahay, Thorbjørnsen & Shavitt — Getting too personal
method_sample: Two experiments; Study 1 N=86; Study 2 N=354 recruited, final N=331
key_finding: Highly distinctive personalization reduced favorable response when fit was unjustified, especially when perceived utility was low.
limitation: Student and email settings; hypothetical/controlled messages.
ad_mind_use: Require a clear utility rationale before using high-depth personalization.

citation: Ham — Exploring how consumers cope with online behavioral advertising
method_sample: Survey; N=442
key_finding: Persuasion knowledge worked through risk, benefit, and self-efficacy; privacy concerns, reactance, and perceived personalization were associated with avoidance.
limitation: Survey and self-reported coping; causal direction is limited.
ad_mind_use: Track perceived surveillance/reactance, not clicks alone.

citation: Farman, Comello & Edwards — Are Consumers Put off by Retargeted Ads?
method_sample: Experiment; N=280
key_finding: Behavioral targeting had a positive direct purchase-intent effect but a negative indirect path through surveillance, threat, reactance, and ad attitude.
limitation: Single experimental product/ad; indirect effect depends on model and measures.
ad_mind_use: Expose the commercial upside and trust cost as simultaneous outcomes.

citation: Chen, Sun & Liu — Balancing web personalization and consumer privacy concerns
method_sample: Online survey and mediated/moderated model; sample size not visible in accessible text
key_finding: With low privacy concern, personalization increased trust and loyalty; with high concern, reactance became the pathway and privacy concern weakened loyalty.
limitation: Cross-sectional website context; sample details need publisher supplement.
ad_mind_use: Provide personalized and non-personalized modes; do not force one policy.

citation: Lee & Cho — Exploring wear-in and wear-out in web advertising
venue: International Journal of Electronic Marketing and Retailing
method_sample: 2×6 experiment; N=222 students; exposures 1,2,3,5,7,9
key_finding: Repetition had weak main effects but interacted with brand familiarity; unfamiliar brands showed nonlinear wear-in/wear-out patterns.
limitation: Mostly 18–23-year-old students, one product category, forced web-banner exposure.
ad_mind_use: Make caps sensitive to brand familiarity and creative/campaign state.

citation: Schmidt & Eisend — Advertising Repetition: A Meta-Analysis
method_sample: Meta-analysis of controlled experimental repetition studies
key_finding: Experimental brand attitude peaked near ten exposures; recall rose through at least eight; spacing, involvement, embedding, and delay moderated effects.
limitation: Experimental optimum is not a production cap; field exposure and creative variation differ.
ad_mind_use: Reject a universal three-exposure rule; tune multi-level caps empirically.

citation: McCoy, Everard, Galletta & Moody — Here we go again!
method_sample: Simulated Chilean website experiment with real ads
key_finding: Repetition degraded ad/site perceptions except when initial ad perceptions were positive; negative ad perceptions reduced revisit intentions as impressions rose.
limitation: Simulated website and country-specific sample; not video or longitudinal behavior.
ad_mind_use: Include host-site attitude and revisit/abandonment guardrails.

citation: Kronrod & Huber — Ad wearout wearout
venue: International Journal of Research in Marketing
method_sample: Field study, four-wave longitudinal online experiment, and third boundary-condition experiment
key_finding: Frequent repetition raised immediate annoyance, but annoyance decayed while memory persisted; later preference reversal occurred only when the category became relevant.
limitation: Culture/categories and measurement timing can change effects; not a reason to ignore immediate UX harm.
ad_mind_use: Report short- and delayed-horizon outcomes separately.

citation: Craig, Sternthal & Leavitt — Advertising Wearout
method_sample: Two high-repetition print-ad experiments
key_finding: Observed recall wearout was attributable partly to inattention and reactance; controlling them removed the decline.
limitation: Old print experiments at extreme repetition levels.
ad_mind_use: Model attention and reactance as mechanisms rather than only impression count.

citation: Rhuggenaath, Akcay, Zhang & Kaymak — Optimal display-ad allocation with guaranteed contracts and SSPs
method_sample: Two-stage stochastic-programming model and numerical experiments against an industry heuristic
key_finding: Publishers must allocate qualifying impressions to guaranteed contracts while deciding what to sell through SSPs; optimal value depends on traffic and required contract share.
limitation: Display-ad SME setting and numerical evaluation, not Tencent or video UX.
ad_mind_use: Model minimum delivery, remaining supply, auction alternative, and shortfall risk.

citation: Cohen, Désir, Korula & Sivan — Best of Both Worlds Ad Contracts
method_sample: Mechanism-design and auction analysis of guaranteed allocation/price with programmatic efficiency
key_finding: Guaranteed contracts can remove allocation and price uncertainty for risk-averse advertisers while coexisting with auction efficiency.
limitation: Theoretical market design; no viewer-experience objective.
ad_mind_use: Represent reserved/guaranteed demand as a valid business constraint, not merely a high bid.

citation: Ali et al. — Discrimination through Optimization
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
method_sample: Black-box Facebook ad-delivery experiments including employment and housing ads
key_finding: Budget, content, market costs, and predicted relevance produced gender/race delivery skew even with neutral or inclusive targeting.
limitation: One platform/time period and inferred demographic outcomes; external audits cannot see internal mechanisms.
ad_mind_use: Audit outcome distribution even when targeting inputs look neutral.

citation: Imana, Korolova & Heidemann — Auditing for Discrimination in Algorithms Delivering Job Ads
method_sample: Paired concurrent-ad black-box audit of Facebook and LinkedIn
key_finding: The method found non-qualification gender skew on Facebook but not LinkedIn, demonstrating the need to separate qualification from delivery optimization.
limitation: Employment domain and U.S. legal framing; audit power depends on platform observability.
ad_mind_use: Add paired counterfactual audit fixtures and category-specific safeguards.

citation: Rathee, Banker, Mishra & Mishra — Algorithms propagate gender bias in the marketplace
method_sample: Large text-corpus analyses plus marketplace/consumer experiments
key_finding: Algorithms reproduced gender associations and consumers reinforced biased delivery by clicking stereotyped ads.
limitation: Focus on gender associations and selected marketplaces; click behavior does not fully define preference.
ad_mind_use: Prevent engagement feedback from silently legitimizing stereotype amplification.

citation: Su, Guo, Tang & Huang — Countdown timers improve online video advertising effectiveness
method_sample: Four lab and eye-tracking experiments
key_finding: Countdowns improved memory for short and long ads, especially experience ads; the mechanism was attention rather than reduced irritation.
limitation: Controlled experiments and memory outcomes; does not contradict context-specific timer irritation effects.
ad_mind_use: Treat attention gain and irritation reduction as different hypotheses.
